description: USBLC6-2 (STMicroelectronics, Doc ID 11265 Rev 5): very low capacitance 2-line ESD protection with VBUS protection for USB 2.0 / Ethernet; USBLC6-2SC6 is the SOT23-6L variant (Fig. 1, Table 5).

pinout.name: I/O1
pinout.notes: Fig. 1 functional diagram (top view): pins 1 and 6 are both I/O1 (internally common); one data line (e.g. D+) connects to pin 1 or 6 and runs straight through to the other side.

pinout.name: GND
pinout.notes: Connect to the PCB GND plane with a track as short as possible (Sec 2.3).

pinout.name: I/O2
pinout.notes: Pins 3 and 4 are both I/O2 (internally common); second data line (e.g. D-).

pinout.name: VBUS
pinout.notes: VBUS protection pin: connect to the VCC/VBUS rail with a track as short as possible (Sec 2.3). Breakdown VBR >= 6 V at 1 mA between VBUS and GND (Table 2). No decoupling capacitor is specified.

land_pattern.package: SOT23-6L recommended footprint (Fig. 22, p.12); body D 2.80-3.05 x E 1.50-1.75 mm, H 2.60-3.00 mm incl. leads, pitch e 0.95 mm (Table 4)
land_pattern.notes: Fig. 22 'footprint dimensions in mm': pad width 0.60, pitch 0.95, pad length 1.20 (upper row dimension line) and 1.10 (lower row dimension line - drawing shows both rows the same size, so 1.2 used for both), overall outer span 3.50, 2.30 labelled between pad rows (taken as pad-centre row spacing, consistent with 3.50-1.20). No courtyard given.

layout_notes: Place the device as close as possible to the disturbance source, i.e. the USB connector (Sec 2.3 'Important').

Rail-to-rail topology: the tracks from data lines to the I/O pins, from VCC/VBUS to the VBUS pin and from the GND plane to the GND pin must all be as short as possible to avoid overvoltage from parasitic inductance (Sec 2.3, Fig. 6/7).

Quantified: 10 mm x 0.5 mm tracks give about 6 nH each; at IEC 61000-4-2 dI/dt of 24 A/ns each adds about 144 V, so clamping rises from +31.2 V to about +319 V (Sec 2.2) - an unsuitable layout defeats the protection.
Fig. 7 optimized layout: route each data line directly through the I/O pin pair (pin 1 to 6, pin 3 to 4) rather than stubbing off the trace; do not branch the line to the device with a long stub.
GND pin 2 should go to the ground plane with a short, preferably direct via/track; VBUS pin 5 to the connector VBUS with a short track.
Capacitance is very low (Ci/o-GND 2.5 pF typ, 3.5 pF max, matching 0.015 pF) so the part suits USB 2.0 high speed (480 Mb/s); keep the D+/D- pair balanced through the device.
Crosstalk between the two lines is below -55 dB up to 240 MHz (Sec 2.4); no extra spacing rule is given.
